research_scope: Source-free, mathematically type-aware audit of shared prerequisites; no source edits and no broad Batch143 population.

aliases.reason: Both the component-union classification of Spec(R) and the clopen-spectrum classification invoke the same idempotent ring element e∈R satisfying e²=e. An ideal generated by idempotents and a single clopen idempotent are distinct higher constructions; the shared prerequisite is exactly elementwise idempotency.

The connected-space and connected-topological-space variants both refer to a subset of a fixed topological space simultaneously open and closed in that ambient topology. The parent connectedness statements differ on whether the empty space is admitted; clopen does not resolve that discrepancy.

Hausdorff separation invokes open neighborhoods of distinct points, and the continuity pointwise criterion invokes open neighborhoods of image and source points. The common prerequisite is an open subset containing a specified point; ordinary neighborhoods that merely contain an open subset remain distinct.

The nilpotent-ideal source uses the positive integral ideal power I^n, and pure-ideal/completion sources use ideal multiplication IJ and its iterations I^n. Both depend on ordinary ideal multiplication in a ring, while the choice of n and nilpotence equation I^n=0 are parent hypotheses.

Finite locally free modules use M_f≅R_f^n over the localized ring R_f, and the filtered-colimit/presentation sources use finite-rank free R-modules R^n. They share finite free rank-n module construction over a unital base ring; localized base and rank varying with chart are parent-specific.
